tagline: A small Markdown-to-HTML renderer for Node.js and browsers.

include: a minimal Markdown input that shows the problem

supported.note: Current line. All fixes land here first.

outOfScope: XSS in HTML you pass through with html: true and do not sanitize, when no advisory names it
slow rendering of documents larger than the maxLength you set

advisories.summary: Cross-site scripting through link titles when html is enabled
advisories.details: When the html option is true, lanternmd copied the title of a Markdown link into the title attribute without escaping quotes. Input such as [x](https://a.example "a" onmouseover="alert(1)") produced an extra attribute. Rendering with html: false (the default) escapes titles and is not affected.

affectedWhen: the Markdown comes from people you do not trust
notAffectedWhen: html is false or unset (the default)
the rendered HTML goes through a sanitizer such as DOMPurify before it reaches a page
only your own authors write the Markdown
desk.vexHint: not_affected with vulnerable_code_not_in_execute_path when html is off; inline_mitigations_already_exist when output is sanitized

advisories.summary: Regular expression denial of service in the emphasis parser
advisories.details: Long runs of underscores and asterisks without a closing marker made the emphasis parser backtrack, taking seconds per kilobyte. The maxLength option, added in 2.3.0, caps the input length and limits the cost. 3.2.0 replaces the pattern with a linear scanner; 2.4.2 backports it. 1.x is end of life and gets no fix.

affectedWhen: untrusted users can submit Markdown and you render it on a server
no maxLength is set, or it is above 20000
notAffectedWhen: you render only in the visitor's own browser, so a slow page affects only them
maxLength is set to 20000 or less (2.3.0 and later)
only trusted authors write the Markdown
workarounds: render in a worker with a timeout
desk.vexHint: not_affected with vulnerable_code_cannot_be_controlled_by_adversary for trusted input; inline_mitigations_already_exist with maxLength 20000 or less

advisories.summary: Prototype pollution through front matter keys
advisories.details: With frontMatter: true, a front matter key named __proto__ or constructor.prototype was merged into the options object, so a document could change defaults for later renders in the same process. Only 3.0.0 to 3.0.4 parse front matter this way.

affectedWhen: the documents come from people you do not trust
one process renders documents from several users
notAffectedWhen: frontMatter is false or unset (the default)
every render runs in a fresh process or worker
workarounds: set frontMatter: false and parse front matter yourself with a safe parser
desk.vexHint: not_affected with vulnerable_code_not_in_execute_path when frontMatter is off
